ESV.1: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.2: “Make two silver trumpets. Of hammered work you shall make them, and you shall use them for summoning the congregation and for breaking camp.
ESV.3: And when both are blown, all the congregation shall gather themselves to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
ESV.4: But if they blow only one, then the chiefs, the heads of the tribes of Israel, shall gather themselves to you.
ESV.5: When you blow an alarm, the camps that are on the east side shall set out.
ESV.6: And when you blow an alarm the second time, the camps that are on the south side shall set out. An alarm is to be blown whenever they are to set out.
ESV.7: But when the assembly is to be gathered together, you shall blow a long blast, but you shall not sound an alarm.
ESV.8: And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. The trumpets shall be to you for a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
ESV.9: And when you go to war in your land against the adversary who oppresses you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, that you may be remembered before the LORD your God, and you shall be saved from your enemies.
ESV.10: On the day of your gladness also, and at your appointed feasts and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings. They shall be a reminder of you before your God: I am the LORD your God.”
ESV.11: In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from over the tabernacle of the testimony,
ESV.12: and the people of Israel set out by stages from the wilderness of Sinai. And the cloud settled down in the wilderness of Paran.
ESV.13: They set out for the first time at the command of the LORD by Moses.
ESV.14: The standard of the camp of the people of Judah set out first by their companies, and over their company was Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
ESV.15: And over the company of the tribe of the people of Issachar was Nethanel the son of Zuar.
ESV.16: And over the company of the tribe of the people of Zebulun was Eliab the son of Helon.
ESV.17: And when the tabernacle was taken down, the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who carried the tabernacle, set out.
ESV.18: And the standard of the camp of Reuben set out by their companies, and over their company was Elizur the son of Shedeur.
ESV.19: And over the company of the tribe of the people of Simeon was Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
ESV.20: And over the company of the tribe of the people of Gad was Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
ESV.21: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things, and the tabernacle was set up before their arrival.
ESV.22: And the standard of the camp of the people of Ephraim set out by their companies, and over their company was Elishama the son of Ammihud.
ESV.23: And over the company of the tribe of the people of Manasseh was Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
ESV.24: And over the company of the tribe of the people of Benjamin was Abidan the son of Gideoni.
ESV.25: Then the standard of the camp of the people of Dan, acting as the rear guard of all the camps, set out by their companies, and over their company was Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
ESV.26: And over the company of the tribe of the people of Asher was Pagiel the son of Ochran.
ESV.27: And over the company of the tribe of the people of Naphtali was Ahira the son of Enan.
ESV.28: This was the order of march of the people of Israel by their companies, when they set out.
ESV.29: And Moses said to Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will do good to you, for the LORD has promised good to Israel.”
ESV.30: But he said to him, “I will not go. I will depart to my own land and to my kindred.”
ESV.31: And he said, “Please do not leave us, for you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you will serve as eyes for us.
ESV.32: And if you do go with us, whatever good the LORD will do to us, the same will we do to you.”
ESV.33: So they set out from the mount of the LORD three days' journey. And the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them three days' journey, to seek out a resting place for them.
ESV.34: And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day, whenever they set out from the camp.
ESV.35: And whenever the ark set out, Moses said, “Arise, O LORD, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee before you.”
ESV.36: And when it rested, he said, “Return, O LORD, to the ten thousand thousands of Israel.”

NASB.1: The LORD spoke further to Moses, saying,
NASB.2: 'Make yourself two trumpets of silver, of hammered work you shall make them; and you shall use them for summoning the congregation and for having the camps set out.
NASB.3: 'When both are blown, all the congregation shall gather themselves to you at the doorway of the tent of meeting.
NASB.4: 'Yet if [only] one is blown, then the leaders, the heads of the divisions of Israel, shall assemble before you.
NASB.5: 'But when you blow an alarm, the camps that are pitched on the east side shall set out.
NASB.6: 'When you blow an alarm the second time, the camps that are pitched on the south side shall set out; an alarm is to be blown for them to set out.
NASB.7: 'When convening the assembly, however, you shall blow without sounding an alarm.
NASB.8: 'The priestly sons of Aaron, moreover, shall blow the trumpets; and this shall be for you a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
NASB.9: 'When you go to war in your land against the adversary who attacks you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, that you may be remembered before the LORD your God, and be saved from your enemies.
NASB.10: 'Also in the day of your gladness and in your appointed feasts, and on the first [days] of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be as a reminder of you before your God. I am the LORD your God.'
NASB.11: Now in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, the cloud was lifted from over the tabernacle of the testimony;
NASB.12: and the sons of Israel set out on their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai. Then the cloud settled down in the wilderness of Paran.
NASB.13: So they moved out for the first time according to the commandment of the LORD through Moses.
NASB.14: The standard of the camp of the sons of Judah, according to their armies, set out first, with Nahshon the son of Amminadab, over its army,
NASB.15: and Nethanel the son of Zuar, over the tribal army of the sons of Issachar;
NASB.16: and Eliab the son of Helon over the tribal army of the sons of Zebulun.
NASB.17: Then the tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who were carrying the tabernacle, set out.
NASB.18: Next the standard of the camp of Reuben, according to their armies, set out with Elizur the son of Shedeur, over its army,
NASB.19: and Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai over the tribal army of the sons of Simeon,
NASB.20: and Eliasaph the son of Deuel was over the tribal army of the sons of Gad.
NASB.21: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy [objects]; and the tabernacle was set up before their arrival.
NASB.22: Next the standard of the camp of the sons of Ephraim, according to their armies, was set out, with Elishama the son of Ammihud over its army,
NASB.23: and Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur over the tribal army of the sons of Manasseh;
NASB.24: and Abidan the son of Gideoni over the tribal army of the sons of Benjamin.
NASB.25: Then the standard of the camp of the sons of Dan, according to their armies, [which formed] the rear guard for all the camps, set out, with Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai over its army,
NASB.26: and Pagiel the son of Ochran over the tribal army of the sons of Asher;
NASB.27: and Ahira the son of Enan over the tribal army of the sons of Naphtali.
NASB.28: This was the order of march of the sons of Israel by their armies as they set out.
NASB.29: Then Moses said to Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, 'We are setting out to the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you'; come with us and we will do you good, for the LORD has promised good concerning Israel.'
NASB.30: But he said to him, 'I will not come, but rather will go to my [own] land and relatives.'
NASB.31: Then he said, 'Please do not leave us, inasmuch as you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you will be as eyes for us.
NASB.32: 'So it will be, if you go with us, that whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do for you.'
NASB.33: Thus they set out from the mount of the LORD three days' journey, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD journeying in front of them for the three days, to seek out a resting place for them.
NASB.34: The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
NASB.35: Then it came about when the ark set out that Moses said, 'Rise up, O LORD! And let Your enemies be scattered, And let those who hate You flee before You.'
NASB.36: When it came to rest, he said, 'Return, O LORD, [To] the myriad thousands of Israel.'

NKJV.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NKJV.2: “Make two silver trumpets for yourself; you shall make them of hammered work; you shall use them for calling the congregation and for directing the movement of the camps.
NKJV.3: When they blow both of them, all the congregation shall gather before you at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
NKJV.4: But if they blow only one, then the leaders, the heads of the divisions of Israel, shall gather to you.
NKJV.5: When you sound the advance, the camps that lie on the east side shall then begin their journey.
NKJV.6: When you sound the advance the second time, then the camps that lie on the south side shall begin their journey; they shall sound the call for them to begin their journeys.
NKJV.7: And when the assembly is to be gathered together, you shall blow, but not sound the advance.
NKJV.8: The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets; and these shall be to you as an ordinance forever throughout your generations.
NKJV.9: “When you go to war in your land against the enemy who oppresses you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God, and you will be saved from your enemies.
NKJV.10: Also in the day of your gladness, in your appointed feasts, and at the beginning of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be a memorial for you before your God: I am the LORD your God.”
NKJV.11: Now it came to pass on the twentieth day of the second month, in the second year, that the cloud was taken up from above the tabernacle of the Testimony.
NKJV.12: And the children of Israel set out from the Wilderness of Sinai on their journeys; then the cloud settled down in the Wilderness of Paran.
NKJV.13: So they started out for the first time according to the command of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
NKJV.14: The standard of the camp of the children of Judah set out first according to their armies; over their army was Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
NKJV.15: Over the army of the tribe of the children of Issachar was Nethanel the son of Zuar.
NKJV.16: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Zebulun was Eliab the son of Helon.
NKJV.17: Then the tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set out, carrying the tabernacle.
NKJV.18: And the standard of the camp of Reuben set out according to their armies; over their army was Elizur the son of Shedeur.
NKJV.19: Over the army of the tribe of the children of Simeon was Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
NKJV.20: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Gad was Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
NKJV.21: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. (The tabernacle would be prepared for their arrival.)
NKJV.22: And the standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim set out according to their armies; over their army was Elishama the son of Ammihud.
NKJV.23: Over the army of the tribe of the children of Manasseh was Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
NKJV.24: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Benjamin was Abidan the son of Gideoni.
NKJV.25: Then the standard of the camp of the children of Dan (the rear guard of all the camps) set out according to their armies; over their army was Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
NKJV.26: Over the army of the tribe of the children of Asher was Pagiel the son of Ocran.
NKJV.27: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Naphtali was Ahira the son of Enan.
NKJV.28: Thus was the order of march of the children of Israel, according to their armies, when they began their journey.
NKJV.29: Now Moses said to Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well; for the LORD has promised good things to Israel.”
NKJV.30: And he said to him, “I will not go, but I will depart to my own land and to my relatives.”
NKJV.31: So Moses said, “Please do not leave, inasmuch as you know how we are to camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
NKJV.32: And it shall be, if you go with us—indeed it shall be—that whatever good the LORD will do to us, the same we will do to you.”
NKJV.33: So they departed from the mountain of the LORD on a journey of three days; and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them for the three days’ journey, to search out a resting place for them.
NKJV.34: And the cloud of the LORD was above them by day when they went out from the camp.
NKJV.35: So it was, whenever the ark set out, that Moses said:  “Rise up, O LORD! Let Your enemies be scattered, And let those who hate You flee before You.”
NKJV.36: And when it rested, he said: “Return, O LORD, To the many thousands of Israel.”

NLT.1: Now the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.2: “Make two trumpets of hammered silver for calling the community to assemble and for signaling the breaking of camp.
NLT.3: When both trumpets are blown, everyone must gather before you at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
NLT.4: But if only one trumpet is blown, then only the leaders — the heads of the clans of Israel — must present themselves to you.
NLT.5: “When you sound the signal to move on, the tribes camped on the east side of the Tabernacle must break camp and move forward.
NLT.6: When you sound the signal a second time, the tribes camped on the south will follow. You must sound short blasts as the signal for moving on.
NLT.7: But when you call the people to an assembly, blow the trumpets with a different signal.
NLT.8: Only the priests, Aaron’s descendants, are allowed to blow the trumpets. This is a permanent law for you, to be observed from generation to generation.
NLT.9: “When you arrive in your own land and go to war against your enemies who attack you, sound the alarm with the trumpets. Then the LORD your God will remember you and rescue you from your enemies.
NLT.10: Blow the trumpets in times of gladness, too, sounding them at your annual festivals and at the beginning of each month. And blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. The trumpets will remind your God of his covenant with you. I am the LORD your God.”
NLT.11: In the second year after Israel’s departure from Egypt — on the twentieth day of the second month — the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle of the Covenant.
NLT.12: So the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai and traveled on from place to place until the cloud stopped in the wilderness of Paran.
NLT.13: When the people set out for the first time, following the instructions the LORD had given through Moses,
NLT.14: Judah’s troops led the way. They marched behind their banner, and their leader was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
NLT.15: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Issachar, led by Nethanel son of Zuar,
NLT.16: and the troops of the tribe of Zebulun, led by Eliab son of Helon.
NLT.17: Then the Tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonite and Merarite divisions of the Levites were next in the line of march, carrying the Tabernacle with them.
NLT.18: Reuben’s troops went next, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Elizur son of Shedeur.
NLT.19: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Simeon, led by Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,
NLT.20: and the troops of the tribe of Gad, led by Eliasaph son of Deuel.
NLT.21: Next came the Kohathite division of the Levites, carrying the sacred objects from the Tabernacle. Before they arrived at the next camp, the Tabernacle would already be set up at its new location.
NLT.22: Ephraim’s troops went next, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Elishama son of Ammihud.
NLT.23: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Manasseh, led by Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,
NLT.24: and the troops of the tribe of Benjamin, led by Abidan son of Gideoni.
NLT.25: Dan’s troops went last, marching behind their banner and serving as the rear guard for all the tribal camps. Their leader was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
NLT.26: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Asher, led by Pagiel son of Ocran,
NLT.27: and the troops of the tribe of Naphtali, led by Ahira son of Enan.
NLT.28: This was the order in which the Israelites marched, division by division.
NLT.29: One day Moses said to his brother-in-law, Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, “We are on our way to the place the LORD promised us, for he said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised wonderful blessings for Israel!”
NLT.30: But Hobab replied, “No, I will not go. I must return to my own land and family.”
NLT.31: “Please don’t leave us,” Moses pleaded. “You know the places in the wilderness where we should camp. Come, be our guide.
NLT.32: If you do, we’ll share with you all the blessings the LORD gives us.”
NLT.33: They marched for three days after leaving the mountain of the LORD, with the Ark of the LORD’s Covenant moving ahead of them to show them where to stop and rest.
NLT.34: As they moved on each day, the cloud of the LORD hovered over them.
NLT.35: And whenever the Ark set out, Moses would shout, “Arise, O LORD, and let your enemies be scattered! Let them flee before you!”
NLT.36: And when the Ark was set down, he would say, “Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel!”

WEB.2: “Make two trumpets of silver. You shall make them of beaten work. You shall use them for the calling of the congregation, and for the journeying of the camps.
WEB.3: When they blow them, all the congregation shall gather themselves to you at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
WEB.4: If they blow just one, then the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather themselves to you.
WEB.5: When you blow an alarm, the camps that lie on the east side shall go forward.
WEB.6: When you blow an alarm the second time, the camps that lie on the south side shall go forward. They shall blow an alarm for their journeys.
WEB.7: But when the assembly is to be gathered together, you shall blow, but you shall not sound an alarm.
WEB.8: “The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be to you for a statute forever throughout your generations.
WEB.9: When you go to war in your land against the adversary who oppresses you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets. Then you will be remembered before Yahweh your God, and you will be saved from your enemies.
WEB.10: “Also in the day of your gladness, and in your set feasts, and in the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be to you for a memorial before your God. I am Yahweh your God.”
WEB.11: In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the testimony.
WEB.12: The children of Israel went forward according to their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud stayed in the wilderness of Paran.
WEB.13: They first went forward according to the commandment of Yahweh by Moses.
WEB.14: First, the standard of the camp of the children of Judah went forward according to their armies. Nahshon the son of Amminadab was over his army.
WEB.15: Nethanel the son of Zuar was over the army of the tribe of the children of Issachar.
WEB.16: Eliab the son of Helon was over the army of the tribe of the children of Zebulun.
WEB.17: The tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who bore the tabernacle, went forward.
WEB.18: The standard of the camp of Reuben went forward according to their armies. Elizur the son of Shedeur was over his army.
WEB.19: Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai was over the army of the tribe of the children of Simeon.
WEB.20: Eliasaph the son of Deuel was over the army of the tribe of the children of Gad.
WEB.21: The Kohathites set forward, bearing the sanctuary. The others set up the tabernacle before they arrived.
WEB.22: The standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim set forward according to their armies. Elishama the son of Ammihud was over his army.
WEB.23: Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur was over the army of the tribe of the children of Manasseh.
WEB.24: Abidan the son of Gideoni was over the army of the tribe of the children of Benjamin.
WEB.25: The standard of the camp of the children of Dan, which was the rear guard of all the camps, set forward according to their armies. Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai was over his army.
WEB.26: Pagiel the son of Ochran was over the army of the tribe of the children of Asher.
WEB.27: Ahira the son of Enan was over the army of the tribe of the children of Naphtali.
WEB.28: Thus were the travels of the children of Israel according to their armies; and they went forward.
WEB.29: Moses said to Hobab, the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are journeying to the place of which Yahweh said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well; for Yahweh has spoken good concerning Israel.”
WEB.30: He said to him, “I will not go; but I will depart to my own land, and to my relatives.”
WEB.31: He said, “Don’t leave us, please; because you know how we are to encamp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
WEB.32: It shall be, if you go with us, yes, it shall be, that whatever good Yahweh does to us, we will do the same to you.”
WEB.33: They set forward from the Mount of Yahweh three days’ journey. The ark of Yahweh’s covenant went before them three days’ journey, to seek out a resting place for them.
WEB.34: The cloud of Yahweh was over them by day, when they set forward from the camp.
WEB.35: When the ark went forward, Moses said, “Rise up, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered! Let those who hate you flee before you!”
WEB.36: When it rested, he said, “Return, Yahweh, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.”

AMP.1: The LORD spoke further to Moses, saying,
AMP.2: "Make two trumpets of silver; you shall make them of hammered work. You shall use them to summon the congregation and to have the camps move out.
AMP.3: When both are blown, all the congregation [that is, all adult males] shall gather before you at the doorway of the Tent of Meeting (tabernacle).
AMP.4: However, if a single trumpet is blown, then the leaders, heads of the tribes of Israel, shall gather themselves to you.
AMP.5: When you blow an alarm, the camps on the east side [of the tabernacle] shall set out.
AMP.6: When you blow an alarm the second time, then the camps on the south side [of the tabernacle] shall set out. They shall blow an alarm whenever they are to move out [on their journeys].
AMP.7: When the assembly is to be gathered, you shall blow [the trumpets in short, sharp tones], but without sounding an alarm.
AMP.8: The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets; and the trumpets shall be for you a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
AMP.9: When you go to war in your land against the enemy that attacks you, then sound an alarm with the trumpets, so that you may be remembered before the LORD your God, and you shall be saved from your enemies.
AMP.10: Also in the day of rejoicing, and in your appointed feasts, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifice of your peace offerings; and they shall be as a reminder of you before your God. I am the LORD your God."
AMP.11: On the twentieth day of the second month in the second year [since leaving Egypt], the cloud [of the Lord's presence] was lifted from over the tabernacle of the Testimony,
AMP.12: and the Israelites set out on their journey from the Wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud [of the Lord's guiding presence] settled down in the Wilderness of Paran.
AMP.13: So they moved out for the first time in accordance with the command of the LORD through Moses.
AMP.14: The standard of the camp of the sons of Judah, according to their armies, moved out first, Nahshon the son of Amminadab was [commander] over its army,
AMP.15: and Nethanel the son of Zuar was [commander] over the tribal army of the sons of Issachar;
AMP.16: and Eliab the son of Helon was [commander] over the tribal army of the sons of Zebulun.
AMP.17: Then the tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who were carrying the tabernacle, moved out.
AMP.18: Next the standard of the camp of the sons of Reuben, according to their armies, moved out, with Elizur the son of Shedeur [commander] over its army,
AMP.19: and Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai was [commander] over the tribal army of the sons of Simeon,
AMP.20: and Eliasaph the son of Deuel was [commander] over the tribal army of the sons of Gad.
AMP.21: Then the Kohathites moved out, carrying the holy things, and the tabernacle was set up before they arrived.
AMP.22: Next the standard of the camp of the sons of Ephraim moved out, according to their armies, with Elishama the son of Ammihud [commander] over its army,
AMP.23: and Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur was [commander] over the tribal army of the sons of Manasseh,
AMP.24: and Abidan the son of Gideoni was [commander] over the tribal army of the sons of Benjamin.
AMP.25: Then the standard of the camp of the sons of Dan, according to their armies, which formed the rear guard for all the camps, moved out, with Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai [commander] over its army,
AMP.26: and Pagiel the son of Ochran was [commander] over the tribal army of the sons of Asher,
AMP.27: and Ahira the son of Enan was [commander] over the tribal army of the sons of Naphtali.
AMP.28: This was the order of march of the sons of Israel by their armies as they moved out.
AMP.29: Then Moses said to Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are going to the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will be good to you, for the LORD has promised good [things] concerning Israel."
AMP.30: But Hobab [Moses' brother-in-law] said to him, "I will not go; I will return to my own land and to my family."
AMP.31: Then Moses said, " Please do not leave us, for you know how we are to camp in the wilderness, and you will serve as eyes for us [as we make our trek through the desert].
AMP.32: So if you will go with us, it shall be that whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do the same for you."
AMP.33: So they set out from the mountain of the LORD (Sinai) three days' journey; and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went in front of them during the three days' journey to seek out a resting place for them.
AMP.34: The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
AMP.35:
Whenever the ark set out, Moses said,
"Rise up, O LORD!
Let Your enemies be scattered;
And let those who hate You flee before You."
AMP.36:
And when the ark rested, Moses said,
"Return, O LORD,
To the myriad (many) thousands of Israel."

MSG.2: "Make two bugles of hammered silver. Use them to call the congregation together and give marching orders to the camps.
MSG.3: When you blow them, the whole community will meet you at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
MSG.4: "When a bugle gives a single, short blast, that's the signal for the leaders, the heads of the clans, to assemble.
MSG.5: When it gives a long blast, that's the signal to march. At the first blast the tribes who were camped on the east set out.
MSG.6: At the second blast the camps on the south set out. The long blasts are the signals to march.
MSG.7: The bugle call that gathers the assembly is different from the signal to march.
MSG.8: "The sons of Aaron, the priests, are in charge of blowing the bugles; it's their assigned duty down through the generations.
MSG.9: When you go to war against an aggressor, blow a long blast on the bugle so that God will notice you and deliver you from your enemies.
MSG.10: Also at times of celebration, at the appointed feasts and New Moon festivals, blow the bugles over your Whole-Burnt-Offerings and Peace-Offerings: they will keep your attention on God. I am God, your God."
MSG.11: In the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, the Cloud went up from over The Dwelling of The Testimony.
MSG.12: At that the People of Israel set out on their travels from the Wilderness of Sinai until the Cloud finally settled in the Wilderness of Paran.
MSG.13: They began their march at the command of God through Moses.
MSG.14: The flag of the camp of Judah led the way, rank after rank under the command of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
MSG.15: Nethanel son of Zuar commanded the forces of the tribe of Issachar,
MSG.16: and Eliab son of Helon commanded the forces of the tribe of Zebulun.
MSG.17: As soon as The Dwelling was taken down, the Gershonites and the Merarites set out, carrying The Dwelling.
MSG.18: The flag of the camp of Reuben was next with Elizur son of Shedeur in command.
MSG.19: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai commanded the forces of the tribe of Simeon;
MSG.20: Eliasaph son of Deuel commanded the forces of the tribe of Gad.
MSG.21: Then the Kohathites left, carrying the holy things. By the time they arrived The Dwelling would be set up.
MSG.22: The flag of the tribe of Ephraim moved out next, commanded by Elishama son of Ammihud.
MSG.23: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur commanded the forces of the tribe of Manasseh;
MSG.24: Abidan son of Gideoni commanded the forces of the tribe of Benjamin.
MSG.25: Finally, under the flag of the tribe of Dan, the rear guard of all the camps marched out with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command.
MSG.26: Pagiel son of Ocran commanded the forces of the tribe of Asher;
MSG.27: Ahira son of Enan commanded the forces of the tribe of Naphtali.
MSG.28: These were the marching units of the People of Israel. They were on their way.
MSG.29: Moses said to his brother-in-law Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We're marching to the place about which God promised, 'I'll give it to you.' Come with us; we'll treat you well. God has promised good things for Israel."

With the Chest leading the way, Moses would say,
Get up, God!
Put down your enemies!
Chase those who hate you to the hills!
MSG.36:
And when the Chest was set down, he would say,
Rest with us, God,
Stay with the many,
Many thousands of Israel.

NET.2: “Make two trumpets of silver; you are to make them from a single hammered piece. You will use them for assembling the community and for directing the traveling of the camps.
NET.3: When they blow them both, all the community must come to you to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

NET.18: The standard of the camp of Reuben set out according to their companies; over his company was Elizur son of Shedeur.
NET.19: Over the company of the tribe of the Simeonites was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,
NET.20: and over the company of the tribe of the Gadites was Eliasaph son of Deuel.

NET.23: Over the company of the tribe of the Manassehites was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,
NET.24: and over the company of the tribe of Benjaminites was Abidan son of Gideoni.

NIV.1:
The Silver Trumpets
The Lord said to Moses:
NIV.2: “Make two trumpets of hammered silver, and use them for calling the community together and for having the camps set out.
NIV.3: When both are sounded, the whole community is to assemble before you at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
NIV.4: If only one is sounded, the leaders—the heads of the clans of Israel—are to assemble before you.
NIV.5: When a trumpet blast is sounded, the tribes camping on the east are to set out.
NIV.6: At the sounding of a second blast, the camps on the south are to set out. The blast will be the signal for setting out.
NIV.7: To gather the assembly, blow the trumpets, but not with the same signal.
NIV.8: “The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to blow the trumpets. This is to be a lasting ordinance for you and the generations to come.
NIV.9: When you go into battle in your own land against an enemy who is oppressing you, sound a blast on the trumpets. Then you will be remembered by the Lord your God and rescued from your enemies.
NIV.10: Also at your times of rejoicing—your appointed feasts and New Moon festivals—you are to sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, and they will be a memorial for you before your God. I am the Lord your God.”
NIV.11:
The Israelites Leave Sinai
On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle of the Testimony.
NIV.12: Then the Israelites set out from the Desert of Sinai and traveled from place to place until the cloud came to rest in the Desert of Paran.
NIV.13: They set out, this first time, at the Lord’s command through Moses.
NIV.14: The divisions of the camp of Judah went first, under their standard. Nahshon son of Amminadab was in command.
NIV.15: Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar,
NIV.16: and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
NIV.17: Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried it, set out.
NIV.18: The divisions of the camp of Reuben went next, under their standard. Elizur son of Shedeur was in command.
NIV.19: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon,
NIV.20: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.
NIV.21: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. The tabernacle was to be set up before they arrived.
NIV.22: The divisions of the camp of Ephraim went next, under their standard. Elishama son of Ammihud was in command.
NIV.23: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh,
NIV.24: and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.
NIV.25: Finally, as the rear guard for all the units, the divisions of the camp of Dan set out, under their standard. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was in command.
NIV.26: Pagiel son of Ocran was over the division of the tribe of Asher,
NIV.27: and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.
NIV.28: This was the order of march for the Israelite divisions as they set out.
NIV.29: Now Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place about which the Lord said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us and we will treat you well, for the Lord has promised good things to Israel.”
NIV.30: He answered, “No, I will not go; I am going back to my own land and my own people.”
NIV.31: But Moses said, “Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the desert, and you can be our eyes.
NIV.32: If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good things the Lord gives us.”
NIV.33: So they set out from the mountain of the Lord and traveled for three days. The ark of the covenant of the Lord went before them during those three days to find them a place to rest.
NIV.34: The cloud of the Lord was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
NIV.35:
Whenever the ark set out, Moses said,
“Rise up, O Lord!
May your enemies be scattered;
may your foes flee before you.”
NIV.36:
Whenever it came to rest, he said,
“Return, O Lord,
to the countless thousands of Israel.”
